article_limitations: Only the 21 completers have individual rows (Table 6); the 7 early discontinuers (reasons given only as counts) have no individual data and are not in the roster.

Table 6 identifies patients only by number: no age, sex, history, medications or comorbidities are stated per patient. PTSD is recorded for each table patient from the abstract statement that the 28 enrolled patients had PTSD; the DSM-5 clinical-interview confirmation is an inclusion requirement and is not recorded as a per-patient diagnostic basis.

Narrative outcome sentences (military PTSD with TBI, childhood trauma, concurrent TMS or ketamine) carry no patient label; they are matched to rows only by identical printed baseline and endpoint values and are kept review only or as ambiguities. For the two 56-point patients (3 and 4) the source does not say which has military and childhood trauma plus TBI.

Follow-up (three patients, including a sequence of PCL-5 values 8 to 0 to 14), booster sessions (four patients), subgroup, strategy-count and bridge-intervention examples (sleep apnea, psychotherapy readiness, suicide risk) are unlabelled and not assigned to roster patients. Cohort statistics and response rates are not copied to individuals.

Discussion calls 85.7% the clinically significant improvement rate, while Results and Table 3 give 90.5% (19/21) for the 10-point threshold and 85.7% (18/21) for the 15-point conservative threshold; recorded here as a source inconsistency at series level, not quarantined in any patient fact.

Figure 1 prints "Did not start (n = 2)" while the text says failure to complete enrollment (n = 2); aggregate only. Figures 2 to 4 give no printed per-patient values and no plot estimates are recorded.
Supplementary Tables S1 and S2 (PDF in a ZIP) are reviewed in the supplement sidecar; Table S1 identifies 11 patients by number with strategy counts and examples.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; actual images are inspected in visual.json.

Discussion describes a patient at high suicide risk after combined TMS, ketamine and Prism, while Methods lists the adjunctive treatment as one patient with TMS and two with ketamine; the source does not identify this patient in Table 6, so nothing is attributed.

Figure 1 prints 'Did not start (n = 2)' among the early discontinuations, while the abstract describes all 28 enrolled patients as treated with Prism; the roster holds only the 21 completers, so this affects no patient record.
